x: The handicap was won by George Stace, with "Jumbo" Masters in second place and Denis Brickwood third, and Masters ran very well seeing that this was his first appearance over the country this season.

We must in the meantime find new blood, possibly in the form of Jumbo Masters and Ron Linstead to strengthen our team and replace our veterans who must inevitably become slower with each succeeding race and who have borne the brunt of this race for so long.
Charlie Walker came in next and so won the Blackstaffe Shield but he only just held off Braughton in the straight. Jumbo Masters came next and Jack Brown only got 3rd Championship medal this year.

Though not fit for beast, the men got on with it until like Jumbo Masters, their feet were crippled. Pirie, Norris and Foord fought it out all the way and our chaps were never in the hunt for the leading positions.
When the time came Jumbo Masters tried to get through the throng to receive the Otway Cup, but it was eventually collected by Peter Bagnall.
The team was not quite as planned as Jumbo Masters still had an injured leg , so Charlie Smart was moved and Eric Gebbett brought into the team.
Second was Pete Bagnall who used his speed to get past Eric Gebbett a mile from home. Eric came third with Jumbo Masters 4th.
Jumbo Masters ran the third fastest time of the day on the Redhill stage to improve our position to 6th. At this stage we were 1 min. 35 secs. down on the leaders Herne Hill.
"Jumbo" Masters never looked at all happy during the early part of the race , but we were most surprised to find that he did not appear at the end of the second lap.
J.Masters · 22.26 · C.Walker · 21.05

Dave Baulch ran well to hold our lead but on the next stage, Len Bishop had to give best to Ellis of T.V.H., and we were now second. A rather unhappy looking 'Jumbo' Masters, whom we welcomed back after a long absence, hung on to our position but we had slipped back on times.
The 5th stage run by Jumbo Masters, saw us drop to 3rd place behind T.V.H. and H.H.H. and our last man, Eric Gebbett, although running well was unable to improve on this.
Then followed a string of runners before we again saw a Belgrave vest filled by Eddie Short who had John Moore and Jumbo Masters close on his heels, all of them in the 130's.

Even Jumbo Masters could do nothing to put the matter right and fell back to 16th with a gap of 5m.55s. between us and Derby. Truly a hopeless position but Alan Black set out to prove that his loss of form over the previous few weeks was purely temporary and with the fifth fastest time of the day br…
Charlie Walker took over five seconds down on the Valley man and in the course of chasing and catching his quarry he passed three others to give 'Jumbo' Masters the baton, in fifth spot.

Don Maclean soon went to the front and looked set for a record breaking run with Charlie Walker, Clive Shippen, Eric Gebbett, John Moore and Jumbo Masters forming one group, twenty yards up on Ranjit Bhatia, Len Bishop and Mike Stearman.
Seven went down for the count, and Jumbo Masters set off in a respectable sixth place. Jumbo had his usual steady run and gained a further position, it was then that Mac had his go!.

Ted Smith, Hugh McGreechan and Charlie Walker are the proud fathers of newly born sons, whilst John Keown and Eric Gebbett and Jumbo Masters are equally proud of their daughters---perhaps we'll have a ladies section yet !

Jumbo Masters, with a time better than two of our 'A' team had gained the 'B' team two places. Don Maclean ran well, despite the agonised look on his face and the jack-tar sway of his body near the finish, but Terry Stacey had taken the Valley back into fourth place.

Heiburg (Woodford) Jumbo Masters, on the next stage, pegged back the previous leaders and so retained 3rd place. Aylesford, after an excellent run by Frank Sando had moved up from 17th to 4th, just behind.

Ken Miller, Jumbo Masters and Symons of Hercules as a result lost 200 yds or so through going off course. Towl (HHH) was a comfortable winner in 29:53, with Shippen (31:30), Miller (31:35) and Masters (31:40), 3rd, 4th, 5th, Charlie Dabbs (34:40) could not overcome the going and finished an uncharacteristic 15th.
Our boys got away to a good start and Black, Miller, Brown, Dabbs and Johnston were soon prominent, with Masters and Dooley further back but well positioned.

We must in the meantime find new blood, possibly in the form of Jumbo Masters and Ron Linstead to strengthen our team and replace our veterans who must inevitably become slower with each succeeding race and who have borne the brunt of this race for so long.
Jumbo Masters.
John Bromley took the 880 yards in 1:59.6 from I.Badiali and Chas. Walker and then the 1 mile in 4:24.8 from 'Jumbo' Masters and Cliff Roffey.
